text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts on hosted API /v2/generate. 5m error rate=6.8% (threshold=1%). Affected cluster: hosted-us-east-1. Pager: P2. Dashboard: https://redwood.app/d/ops/api-errors

alice: I'm taking this incident. on-call handoff acknowledged. pinging eng-runtime and infra.

dennis: on-call (dennis) — I'm here. did we have any recent rollouts in the last 30m?

ben: no deploys in last hour from CI. initial look at edge logs shows lots of 502/504 from gateway (nginx) with upstream reset_by_peer. sample log: `upstream: "http://10.2.3.45:8000"`, status=502, request_time=4.02, upstream_response_time=3.99

farah: adding context — I've seen this pattern when worker KV cache saturates and starts dropping connections. checking model-backend pool metrics and connection error counters.

emma: CS: we have one high-priority ticket from Acme reporting request timeouts ~11:10 UTC, also Slack message to customer success.

carla: product — we should surface list of impacted customers (Acme) and estimate SLO impact.

alice: running quick health checks on internal endpoints. `curl -v https://api.redwood.com/v2/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` -> 502 intermittently.

deploy-bot: deploy-check: No active deployments in the last 60m.

dennis: mitigation plan step 1: scale up hosted-worker pool by +2 nodes and pin routing away from the smaller shared nodes. doing `infractl scale pool hosted-worker --add 2` now.

ben: mitigation step 2: enable fallback routing for non-enterprise tenants to model:small-quantized to reduce backend load. Command: `redwood route update --path /v2/generate --fallback model:small-quant` (applying)

alice: quick hotfix: reverting aggressive batching patch that went live earlier today (commit 0a9f7c3). deploying hotfix-20240731-batching-rollback. Rollout to 10% -> 50% -> 100% with canary; monitoring logs.

ben: can confirm connection errors to model-backend reduced after enabling fallback routing, and scaled nodes are provisioning. There's a spike of 429s for a subset of clients — looks like throttling kicking in on fallback model.

farah: adding temporary alert adjustments: increasing suppression window for this alert group to avoid alert storms while we stabilize. Also setting up live trace to identify heavy clients: `trace --service gateway --filter 'status>=500' --top 20`

emma: flagged impacted customer Acme in status page. Messaging CS team to acknowledge and offer ETA.

alice: error-rate dropping: 5m error rate now 0.9%, 1m rate 1.1%. will keep monitoring for 15m before declaring service restored.

dennis: handoff note for next on-call: if errors reappear after scale down, escalate to infra-team and consider temporary routing to dedicated-downgraded model for enterprise tenants.

carla: product note — customer impact: Acme saw ~40 failed requests, likely below SLA threshold but needs follow-up. adding to incident summary.

ben: small hotfix shipped: changed nginx upstream keepalive on gateway to 30s and increased proxy_read_timeout to 60s. commit: `git+ssh://repo/redwood/infra@b12c3e - tweak gateway timeouts` (deployed to prod-canary then prod).

incident-bot: status update: incidents/errors:5xx on /v2/generate mitigated. 5m error rate -> 0.6%.

alice: confirming mitigations applied: scaling + fallback + rollback + gateway timeout tweaks. two immediate follow-ups to create before we close: 1) runbook update for this failure mode and 2) alerts tuning (include SLO burn-rate and customer list).

farah: agreed. I'll own runbook updates (farah). will add a diagnostic section: "gateway 502s due to kv-cache saturation -> steps: scale pool, enable fallback routing, revert batching patch, increase upstream keepalive/timeouts"

ben: I'll own alerts tuning (ben). proposed changes: - reduce sensitivity of transient 5xx alerts (add short suppression by deployment) - add burn-rate alert tied to SLOs - add per-customer 5xx threshold to page on >100 errors in 15m.

dennis: action item: create a postmortem doc and link to this thread. I'll start the template and assign owners.

carla: product action: reach out to Acme with summary and remediation steps. Emma, can you take point on messaging?

emma: on it. crafting message for Acme now — will include apology and what we changed, and offer 1:1 if they want deeper root-cause details.

alice: putting incident into 'monitoring' state for 15m. if stable -> declare resolved and open follow-up tickets.

deploy-bot: monitor: health check OK.

incident-bot: RESOLVED: Elevated 5xx on /v2/generate mitigated at 1719877043. Root cause: aggressive batching config + gateway timeout sensitivity + temporary kv-cache saturation.

--- FOLLOW-UPS / ACTION ITEMS ---
- FARAH: update runbook with specific mitigation steps and example commands (owner: farah, due: 2024-08-07).
- BEN: tune alerts (add SLO burn-rate alert, per-customer thresholds) and add suppression on deploy windows (owner: ben, due: 2024-08-05).
- DENNIS: create postmortem doc + timeline and link dashboards (owner: dennis, due: 2024-08-06).
- EMMA & CARLA: send customer-facing incident note to Acme and update status page (owners: emma, carla, due: 2024-08-01).
- ALICE: run a load test with new gateway timeout settings and updated batching config in staging and report results (owner: alice, due: 2024-08-02).

alice: thumbs up. closing thread here once follow-ups are created and owners ack. :white_check_mark:

carla: thanks everyone. great fast coordination. :clap:

emma: closing CS loop after follow-up message sent.

incident-bot: thread closed.
